steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage: treated vs control
caveats: STAR+featureCounts counts carry no quantifier-side GC/length bias correction; the conventional correction tools (cqn, EDASeq) are not present in this environment. Draw the log-count-ratio-vs-GC-content diagnostic across sample pairs and report whether a trend is present; do not attempt an in-step correction.

With 3 replicates per group, both the DESeq2 Wald test and any comparable count model have low power and reliably detect only a minority of true effects, mostly with large fold changes. A gene absent from the significant list is not evidence it is unchanged. Do not loosen alpha to compensate.

DESeq2 flags a per-gene count outlier (Cook's distance) and sets its p-value/padj to NA when the affected condition cell has fewer than 7 replicates (true here, n=3); report these NAs separately from the independent-filtering NAs.

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: Bulk RNA-seq, human liver, drug treatment vs control, 3 vs 3, single batch, raw STAR/featureCounts integer gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples; no length correction needed or applied). Flow: (1) sample-structure QC on a blind VST to catch outliers/batch structure before any modeling; (2) minimal count pre-filter; (3) DESeq2 Wald test with an explicit reference level (control) and apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control log2 fold change, BH-adjusted with DESeq2's independent filtering at alpha=0.05; (4) preranked fgsea on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome + WikiPathways (secondary, available in the reference store) with a 15-500 gene-set size window and redundancy collapse; (5) a report that states the DESeq2/apeglm/fgsea diagnostics, the reproducibility record, and — critically — the expected power limitation of an n=3-per-group design (R-0017/R-0094/R-0162): a gene absent from the significant list is not evidence of no effect, and only large fold changes are reliably detectable at this replicate count. No batch correction is applied (single batch, none declared). No GC/length bias correction tool (cqn/EDASeq) is available in this environment for featureCounts data; a GC/length bias diagnostic plot is reported as a caveat rather than corrected.

flags.message: With counts from an aligner and a counter, no bias model runs at the quantification, thus a sample-specific effect of the GC content and of the gene length can remain in the counts, and such an effect adds a difference between samples that the between-sample normalization does not remove. Draw the diagnostic: for each pair of samples, or for each sample against the median sample, plot the log ratio of the counts against the GC content of the genes and against the gene length, and report a trend. For a 3' tag library, the count does not depend on the gene length, thus plot the GC content only. Conditional quantile normalization (cqn) and the GC-content normalization of EDASeq are the tools of record for the correction, and both are absent from this pool. If the diagnostic shows a trend, state it in the plan and ask for cqn, or for a new quantification with a bias-aware quantifier such as Salmon with its GC bias model. If the diagnostic shows no trend, state the check and continue.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
